shared_mechanisms: Team B5 shared mechanisms. M1 'utterance reader' (T10) is also the cue matcher for T01 taxonomy cues and the T35 skill check. M2 'question ledger and policy' (T05) takes the panel's tagged question from T35 and the correction reader from T10. M3 'egress gate' (backend/app/core/egress.py) is one choke point for every outbound call: it enforces the session privacy policy (T25, using T19 purposes), the per-destination limits, concurrency, priority and per-provider usage (T15), and carries the single batched panel call (T35). M4 'keyring' (backend/app/core/crypto.py) provides AES-GCM field encryption and HMAC blind indexes (T30), which T20 also uses to hash programme join codes and enrolment tokens.

designs.understanding: There is no single object that owns the question budget. The 7-question cap is measured as len(session.turns) (session.py:137-139), so the opening pitch, every re-ask and every opinion request each use one up, while REQUIRED_BY_MODE[IDEA] holds 9 slots (every Need.REQUIRED slot in slots.py). Dynamic questions from the scan and the panel skip the selector entirely: engine.step asks them at step 2, before any required slot, through a first-come cap of 3 (engine.py:193-203, 274-285). Their answers are written to d['answer'] and nobody reads them. The selector values a slot by a fixed consumer count (selector.py:83-99), not by what its absence blocks right now. The WHY finger owns no required slot, so the five-finger rule checks four fingers (selector.py:214-222). The restatement names only session.missing, which removes skipped slots (session.py:126-127), and it leaves out the facts the planner uses most (team_size, founder_years, time_horizon). The common cause: asking, skipping and assuming are three unconnected code paths with no ledger and no single policy. So nobody can tell which questions were asked, which facts were assumed, or why a question was worth a turn.

flags_disputed.note: Holds, with one nuance: CP-SAT is solved twice per turn only once required coverage is met. While required slots are unfilled, is_objective_clear returns before calling select_next (selector.py:198-205), so the solver runs once (from next_question). The conclusion stands: at the default horizon and budget the solver never changes the head question.

approaches.name: Question ledger plus one policy (greedy, required-first, quotas), with CP-SAT kept for binding budgets
approaches.how: The session keeps an ordered ledger of AskRecord entries (key, kind slot|dynamic, source, counted, outcome). Every question goes through one QuestionPolicy.next(): a candidate pool holding required slots, a WHY any-of group, tagged dynamic questions (with per-source quotas) and enrichment slots, all scored by one value function that includes a blocked-results term. The budget counts only ledger entries marked counted. Required slots the budget cannot reach become explicit assumptions in the restatement.
approaches.basis: Event-ledger pattern inside the existing session JSON document (0005), plus the existing selector. No new dependency.
approaches.advantages: One decider, so ordering, quotas and budget cannot conflict. The ledger makes skipped and assumed facts visible and testable. Fits decision 0002 (code decides).
approaches.drawbacks: Needs a session format bump (T34) for old documents. The value weights stay uncalibrated.

approaches.name: Full CP-SAT plan over slots and dynamic questions together
approaches.how: Model every candidate (slot and dynamic) as a boolean in one CP-SAT model with budget, quota and ordering constraints, re-solved every turn.
approaches.basis: OR-Tools CP-SAT, already installed and used by selector.py.
approaches.advantages: Expresses quotas and budget as constraints in one formal model.
approaches.drawbacks: The flag's probe shows the solver adds nothing at this problem size, at about 28 ms per turn against 0.04 ms for greedy. Harder to explain and test, and the greedy fallback still needs the same rules.

approaches.name: Expected value of information with answer priors
approaches.how: Score each question by the expected information gain over downstream decisions, using prior distributions over answers.
approaches.advantages: Principled: asks what changes decisions most.
approaches.drawbacks: Needs answer priors per district, sector and stage that do not exist, so they would be invented data. Opaque to founders and to the team.

approaches.name: Separate budgets per question class
approaches.how: Keep turns as they are, and give required slots, dynamic questions and enrichment their own caps (for example 9 + 3 + 2).
approaches.advantages: Trivial to build, with no ordering conflicts.
approaches.drawbacks: Makes interviews longer, which the design explicitly avoids (rnd-elicitation 4.2). Does not fix vanishing assumptions or the value-blind dynamic path.

approaches.name: Static dialogue script (state chart of fixed question order)
approaches.how: Replace the selector with a hand-written order: what, who/where, when, how, then dynamic questions.
approaches.advantages: Predictable and very easy to test.
approaches.drawbacks: Ignores what the pitch already filled and what each gap blocks, and throws away the selector and decision-class modelling already built. Skips still need a ledger.

approaches.name: The model decides the next question (LLM planner)
approaches.how: Ask Gemini or Ollama which question to ask next, given the known facts.
approaches.drawbacks: Contradicts decision 0002 (code decides, the model words). Absent offline and not deterministic, so the eval set cannot pin it.

designs.chosen: Question ledger plus one policy (greedy, required-first, quotas), with CP-SAT kept for binding budgets
designs.why_chosen: It fixes the root cause: no single place decides and records what is asked. It reuses the selector, the slot table and the session document. The ledger gives one source of truth for the 'I skipped / I assumed' restatement, the dynamic-answer binding and the budget unit. It also pairs with the T10 correction reader: the confirmation step becomes a cheap catch-all where the founder can correct any assumed fact in one sentence. That makes a 7-question cap against 9 required slots safe instead of silently wrong.

not_chosen.name: Full CP-SAT plan
not_chosen.reason: Measured to give the same head question as greedy at about 700 times the cost. The budget is a count, which greedy plus a filter handles exactly; the solver stays only for the voice burden budget, where it can bind.

not_chosen.name: Expected value of information
not_chosen.reason: Needs invented answer priors, against the no-invented-data rule.

not_chosen.name: Separate budgets per class
not_chosen.reason: Makes interviews longer, against the product decision, and leaves assumptions invisible.

not_chosen.name: Static dialogue script
not_chosen.reason: Asks about facts the pitch already gave, and discards the decision-class value model.

not_chosen.name: The model decides the next question
not_chosen.reason: Violates decision 0002 and the offline baseline.

design.data_model: ElicitationSession gains asked: list[AskRecord], where AskRecord = {key:str, kind:'slot'|'dynamic', source:'selector'|'scan'|'panel'|'reask'|'repeat', counted:bool, outcome:'pending'|'answered'|'missed'|'skipped'|'corrected', turn:int}. questions_asked = count(counted). A dynamic entry becomes DynamicQ{key, question, source, binds:{'slot':key}|{'criterion':c}|{'note':True}, duplicates_slot:str|None, asked:bool, answer:str|None}. Founder notes: session.notes: list[{text, criterion|None, turn}], with Source.ANSWER provenance through T03's typed put. Slot gains restate:bool (computed: kind != 'text' and consumers include 'roadmap' or 'scheme') and a WHY any-of group: WHY_GROUP = ('why_now','differentiation','motivation').
design.algorithm: next(): (1) a pending re-ask, not counted. (2) Candidates: unfilled required slots; the WHY group (one candidate, 'differentiation', ranked below the required slots) when no WHY slot is filled; dynamic questions whose binding is not yet satisfied (a filled duplicates_slot drops the question), admitted only when the remaining budget exceeds the remaining required count, or after required coverage; enrichment after required coverage. Source quotas: scan at most 1, panel at most 2, and a panel arrival replaces an unasked scan question. (3) Value = question_value + W_BLOCKED * blocked(slot), where blocked() counts scheme rules that are three-valued 'unknown' only because of this slot (interface from T04) plus the roadmap gates that need it; until T04 lands it falls back to len(consumers). Sensitive slots are excluded unless the T19 purpose is granted. (4) Greedy with required-first; select_next (CP-SAT) only when the channel's burden budget binds (voice). (5) Stop when questions_asked >= Q_MAX, or when required slots are covered and the best value < TAU_GAIN. On stop, every required slot not sourced from ANSWER (extracted, defaulted or skipped) goes on the 'assumed' list with the default value from the planner's defaults (T03 and T01 own the default table).
design.interfaces: T03: put() returns an outcome and a source rank; ledger outcomes come from it. T10: the correction reader turns a confirmation reply into slot changes, so assumed facts can be fixed at confirmation without a question. T35: the panel question arrives tagged with criterion and duplicates_slot. T04: unknown_inputs(profile) -> Counter[field] feeds blocked(). T19: purposes gate sensitive slots. T24: experience mode reuses the same policy with its own required set. T34: session format version for the new fields. T27: the typed pending action carries the AskRecord key.
design.rollout: Add the ledger first. Old documents without 'asked' are upgraded by T34's upgrader, which derives entries from turns (counted = asked and not a repeat). Then move step() onto the policy, with no flag; the eval replay set must keep every case that passes today. Then add the restatement parts. Q_MAX stays 7, and 5.1.3 tunes its value later.
design.offline: Fully deterministic, no model. CP-SAT is optional: greedy plus required-first is the complete behaviour.

designs.understanding: Every reading of a founder's reply is a bare substring or set test. _first_cue uses 'n in low' (extract.py _first_cue), so 'app' fires inside Tiruchirappalli, 'crop' inside 'microprocessor' and 'course' inside 'of course'. Yes/no at confirmation is a set intersection (ideation.py:55-56, _advance), so 'not right' contains 'right' and confirms, and 'yes but Salem not Erode' confirms without reading the correction. Nothing handles negation scope ('no customers yet' -> revenue; answers._stage now has a leading \b but still no negation), corrections ('actually', 'not X, Y'), the position or role of a place in a sentence (find_district picks the longest name, not the first or the 'from/in' one), or towns below district level (no Pollachi). Any answer of 25 or more characters also produces a positional 'problem' guess that can overwrite the real problem at equal confidence. The root cause is the missing reading layer between raw text and slot writes: one that tokenises once, matches cues on word boundaries, marks negated and corrected spans, and has its own gazetteer.

approaches.name: Deterministic reading layer: tokens with spans, word-boundary lexicon matcher, negation and correction scopes, role-aware places, pincode-derived gazetteer
approaches.how: elicitation/reading.py tokenises the reply once (regex tokens with character spans, clause breaks at , . ; and 'but'). A Lexicon compiles each cue list into one alternation regex with word boundaries and optional stems ('manufactur\w*'). A NegEx-style trigger list ('no', 'not', 'never', 'without', "haven't", 'illai', 'yet to') marks the following tokens as negated, up to a clause break or 3 tokens. Correction triggers ('actually', 'sorry', 'I meant', 'not X, (it is) Y', 'change X to Y') mark the new value as a correction. Places come from a town gazetteer, with role cues ('in', 'from', 'based in', 'my unit is in' = operating; 'sell in', 'export to' = market) and the earliest operating mention first. Output: Reading{tokens, mentions:[Mention(key, value, span, negated, corrected, role, strength)], polarity}.
approaches.basis: NegEx (Chapman et al. 2001) is the standard rule-based negation method. The India Post all-India pincode directory on data.gov.in (OGD licence) is already cited in the repo (banking/data/branches_tn5.json _meta).
approaches.advantages: Offline, fast, explainable and testable with Hypothesis. One module fixes every flag, and T01 cue lists, T35 skills and T05 confirmation reuse it.
approaches.drawbacks: Rule lists need curation and review. English and transliterated Tamil only at first; Tamil-script cues must be added by review.

design.components: backend/app/elicitation/reading.py (new): tokenize(); Lexicon (compiled word-boundary matcher with stems and multi-word phrases); negation scopes; correction detection; polarity(text) -> YES|NO|YES_WITH_CHANGES|CHANGES|UNCLEAR; read(text, answering) -> Reading. extract.py is rewritten on top of read(), keeping its public extract() -> list[Extraction] shape plus new fields. places.py gains the gazetteer, find_places(text) -> list[PlaceMention(district, name, span, role)] and a find_district() wrapper (earliest operating mention). answers.validate uses read() for stage and enums, with negation. agents/ideation.py _advance uses polarity() and always observes the reply at CONFIRMING, then confirms only if nothing changed.
design.data_model: Mention{key, value, span:(int,int), negated:bool, corrected:bool, role:'operate'|'market'|None, strength:float}. Extraction gains source_hint:'answer'|'correction'|'extracted' and excludes:list (negated values, for example district != madurai). Gazetteer file backend/app/elicitation/data/tn_places.json: {_meta:{source:'India Post all-India pincode directory, data.gov.in, OGD licence', retrieved, licence}, places:{town_lower:[district_id,...]}}, generated by scripts/build_tn_places.py from the published CSV (office name, Taluk, District, StateName == TAMIL NADU), with district names normalised to the 38 ids in places.DISTRICTS. A town in several districts maps to a list; an ambiguous town is not filled but asked.
design.algorithm: Tokens: re.finditer(r"[\w']+|[.,;!?]") over the lower-cased text, with spans. Clause breaks: punctuation and 'but', 'however', 'though'. Negation: a trigger negates the following tokens until a clause break, at most 3 tokens (NegEx window), plus 'X not Y' patterns and post-triggers ('not yet', 'yet to'). Correction: the triggers 'actually', 'sorry', 'i meant', 'instead', 'change', or the contrast 'not X(,) (it is|but) Y' mark Y as corrected and X as excluded. Lexicon match: one compiled regex per key, r'(?<!\w)(?:cue1|cue2|stem\w*)(?!\w)', returning all matches with spans; a sector or form value whose matches are all negated is dropped; with several sectors, the earliest unnegated match wins, ties going to the longest cue. Places: candidates from districts, aliases and the gazetteer; role from the preceding 3 tokens; choose corrected, then operating role, then earliest. The positional 'problem' guess is emitted only when answering is None (a free description), never when the reply answers a slot. Polarity: YES and NO words are counted outside negation scope ('not right' -> NO, 'not wrong' -> YES); YES plus any slot mention -> YES_WITH_CHANGES; NO plus a mention -> CHANGES; NO alone -> NO; otherwise UNCLEAR.
design.interfaces: T01: Lexicon matches the canonical taxonomy cue lists (T01 owns the vocabularies, T10 owns the matching). T03: Extraction.source_hint maps onto T03's source rank (CORRECTION > ANSWER > PROFILE > EXTRACTED), and excludes becomes a typed 'not' fact. T05: polarity and corrections drive confirmation: YES_WITH_CHANGES or CHANGES apply the changes and restate again; NO with no mention asks 'Which part should I change?' listing the restated facts (not counted against the budget). T27: the pending action at CONFIRMING is typed, not inferred from state. T35: the skills check uses Lexicon. T02: tn_places.json carries provenance metadata in T02's format and is checked in CI (T22).
design.rollout: Land reading.py and the Lexicon first, with extract() using them behind the same interface, and run the eval replays plus the new negative set. Then switch answers and places, then confirmation. The gazetteer ships in its own commit with provenance and a CI check that every value is one of the 38 district ids.
design.offline: Entirely offline, standard library only. The gazetteer is a committed file, never fetched at runtime.

designs.understanding: Outbound calls have no governor. research/sources._get_json is already the single function behind every research request, but it lets transport errors escape (client.get with no try), and scan and novelty gather without return_exceptions, so one GitHub timeout fails the whole scan. It returns only (status, text), so 'our own cap', 'the source asked us to wait' and 'the source refused' are all 429, and papers() maps every 429 to 'add OPENALEX_API_KEY'. One daily limit covers all sources (research_daily_limit, default 0), so an 80% alert has no denominator, and GitHub and EPO limits are per minute anyway. On the model side, the panel fires seven parallel judge calls (council/__init__.py) and jobs start immediately (jobs.py start), so bursts hit Gemini's per-minute free quota, open the shared breaker and degrade live turns. Usage is one dict with no provider key, so free local Ollama tokens use up SESSION_TOKEN_BUDGET while the real Gemini daily quota is never counted. The OpenAlex calls in papers() and the scan's element searches run one after another. The root cause: there is no shared egress layer that knows each destination's limits, priority and cost and returns a typed outcome.

approaches.name: In-house egress gate: destination table, typed Outcome reasons, token bucket plus daily counter, priority reserve, per-destination semaphores, per-provider usage
approaches.how: backend/app/core/egress.py holds DESTINATIONS {name: Dest(kind research|model|voice, locality local|cloud, vendor, limits [(n, 'minute'|'day')], concurrency, metered)}, loaded from settings (EGRESS_LIMITS='openalex=100000/day,github=10/min,epo=10/min,gemini=15/min,gemini=1500/day'). gate.call(dest, fn, priority) checks the policy (T25), the minute bucket (in-process, with a reserve that only priority 'live' may use), the day counter (Redis INCR when Redis runs, else in-process) and the semaphore; runs fn; catches httpx.TransportError; records usage; and returns Outcome{dest, reason, status, data, retry_after}. Research and providers both call through it.
approaches.basis: Generalises the existing Redis INCR pattern and the breaker; token bucket and GCRA are standard algorithms. No dependency.
approaches.advantages: One place for every limit, reason, priority and counter. Gives T23 real denominators and T25 one enforcement point. Small (about 200 lines).
approaches.drawbacks: In-process minute buckets undercount across several workers (acceptable: one worker today, and the Redis day counters stay shared).

design.data_model: Reason = OK | CACHED | OWN_CAP | UPSTREAM_PAUSE | UPSTREAM_LIMIT | NO_KEY | TRANSPORT | UPSTREAM_ERROR | POLICY. Outcome{dest, reason, http_status:int|None, data, retry_after:float|None}. SourceResult.status adds 'paused' and 'unreachable' and keeps budget_exhausted only for OWN_CAP and UPSTREAM_LIMIT, each with its own note. Session usage becomes {provider: {input_tokens, output_tokens, requests}}; a T34 upgrader folds the old flat dict into 'unknown'. Redis keys: use:{dest}:{yyyy-mm-dd}:{requests|tokens} (2-day expiry); budget:{source}:{date} stays as an alias during the change.
design.algorithm: call(dest, fn, priority): policy check (T25) -> POLICY; pause key -> UPSTREAM_PAUSE; minute bucket of capacity n per minute with continuous refill, where a caller below priority 'live' takes a token only while tokens > reserve (30% of capacity, configurable); empty bucket -> OWN_CAP with retry_after; the day counter is incremented only when the call is actually sent (fixing the over-count of refused requests), and reaching the limit -> OWN_CAP; semaphore per destination; try fn(), mapping httpx.TransportError -> TRANSPORT, 429 -> pause plus UPSTREAM_LIMIT, other non-200 -> UPSTREAM_ERROR; record requests, tokens (metered only) and outcome. Percent used = day_count / day_limit, defined for every destination that has a day limit; others report 'no daily limit'. Research parallelism: papers() gathers its three OpenAlex requests, scan gathers the per-element searches, novelty gathers its independent waves. Because call() never raises for transport errors, gather needs no return_exceptions, and a failing source only sets its own status.
design.interfaces: T08: the cache lookup stays before gate.call, so a cache hit spends no budget; T08 owns key normalisation and atomic writes. T25: Gate.call consults the session EgressPolicy (local only in private mode). T35: the panel's single call uses priority 'panel'. T23: Gate.usage() and status() feed the observability store and the 80% alert. T12: the job semaphores live in the job board T12 bounds. docs/runbooks/research-budget.md is rewritten per reason.
design.rollout: 1) Typed outcomes and the transport catch in _get_json (no change on the ok path). 2) The gate, with a limits table whose defaults reproduce today's behaviour (no caps) plus documented recommended values. 3) Providers through the gate, with per-provider usage. 4) Parallel research. Each step ships on its own.

designs.understanding: The programme view aggregates whatever list of session ids the caller posts (routers/cohort.py ProgrammeIn, up to 500). It answers every request with exact counts for groups of 5 or more, exact averages and a raw reached_a_roadmap count (programme.py). Anyone can difference two lists, or plant four self-made consenting sessions plus a victim, and read one founder's attributes. The unit counted is the session, not the founder, so restarts count twice. The session id handed to the programme is also the full read, write and delete credential. The endpoint has no auth, and the planned auth needs a database that is not available. The root cause: the caller chooses the membership instead of the server owning it, and disclosure control is a per-field habit (_grouped) instead of one rule applied to every published number.

approaches.name: Server-owned programme membership by join code and enrolment token, one disclosure function (round to 5, suppress 1-4, bands for averages), published snapshots that change only in steps of 5 or more members, and an interim operator key
approaches.how: An operator creates a programme document (id, name, join-code hash, operator-key hash) in the existing store. A founder enters the join code at session start or later; the server records an enrolment {enrolment_id, programme_id, latest_session_id, consent_version} and returns an opaque enrolment token that the browser keeps and resends with new sessions. The programme endpoint takes only programme_id plus the operator key, computes over the latest session per enrolment, passes every number through disclose(), and serves the last published snapshot, which is refreshed only after a membership change of 5 or more.
approaches.basis: Statistical disclosure control practice of national statistics offices (threshold rule and rounding to base 5, as in UK ONS and Statistics Canada small-cell rules); enrolment matches TASKS 5.5.4.
approaches.advantages: Removes caller-chosen sets (the root cause) and session ids from the programme flow, counts founders, and closes differencing across requests and across snapshots. Works today for anonymous founders, with no database.
approaches.drawbacks: Snapshots lag membership changes. A leaked join code still lets someone enrol planted sessions (bounded by rounding and step publication).

approaches.name: Differential privacy (OpenDP or diffprivlib) on the aggregates
approaches.how: Add calibrated Laplace or Gaussian noise to each count and track a privacy budget per programme.
approaches.basis: The formal standard (Dwork 2006); OpenDP and IBM diffprivlib are maintained.
approaches.drawbacks: For batches of 5-30 the noise makes the bands unreadable for the programme manager. Budget accounting is state to keep and hard to explain to an incubator.

approaches.name: Query auditing (overlap control)
approaches.how: Store past queries and refuse a new set that overlaps an earlier one by all but a few members.
approaches.drawbacks: Needs a stored query history and is still evadable with planted sessions. Does not stop session ids being credentials.

approaches.name: Owner-bound sessions and account-based membership
approaches.how: Wait for T17 accounts; membership becomes a users-programmes table and the view requires a programme role.
approaches.drawbacks: Blocked on the database (2.1.1) and T17, and it leaves anonymous founders double counted and exposed meanwhile. Still needs disclosure control.

approaches.name: k-anonymity / microdata tooling (ARX, sdcMicro)
approaches.how: Generalise each founder's record until every combination appears at least k times, then aggregate.
approaches.drawbacks: Built for releasing microdata, not a handful of aggregate counts, and needs a foreign runtime.

approaches.name: Signed cohort token instead of session ids (HMAC capability)
approaches.how: Each founder gets an HMAC token that the programme posts instead of a session id.
approaches.advantages: Stops handing over the full session key.
approaches.drawbacks: The caller still chooses the set, so the differencing leak stays.

design.data_model: Programme document in the store (key 'programme:{id}'): {id, name, join_code_bi (HMAC-SHA256 via the T30 keyring), operator_key_bi, created_at, members: {enrolment_id: {token_bi, latest_session_id, joined_at, consent_record_id}}, published: {at, member_count_rounded, payload, members_at_publish}}. The session document gains enrolment_id, replacing cohort_consent; the T34 upgrader drops the old flag and enrols no one. The enrolment token is 128-bit random and is shown to the browser once (kept in T18's key registry). Consent: a T19 consent record with purpose 'programme_aggregate' and the programme_id.
design.algorithm: disclose_count(n) = 0 if n == 0; 'fewer than 5' if 1 <= n <= 4; else 5*round(n/5). disclose_counts(values) groups the values and applies disclose_count, folding sub-5 groups into one 'fewer than 5' bucket that is itself rounded or suppressed. Shares become bands ('under a quarter', 'about half', ...). founders_listed and founders_sharing are never published exactly; only member_count_rounded is. Publication: recompute nightly (T32 runner) or on operator request, but replace 'published' only when the symmetric difference between current members and members_at_publish is 5 or more; otherwise serve the old snapshot and say when it will update. Nothing is shown below 5 members. Aggregates use the latest session per enrolment.
design.interfaces: T17: once owners exist, an enrolment links user_id and the token becomes optional; the session id never leaves the founder. T19: consent record with purpose and withdrawal; a withdrawal removes the member at the next publication. T30: keyring HMAC for the *_bi fields. T14: require_operator is replaced by a programme role. T32: the maintenance runner publishes snapshots. T18: the browser stores the enrolment token in its key registry. T07: programme documents use the same store, with no idle expiry.
design.rollout: 1) The disclosure function applied to today's endpoint (an immediate partial fix). 2) The operator key on the endpoint. 3) Membership and enrolment, removing the session-id endpoint in the same release. 4) Published snapshots once T32 exists (until then, publish on operator request, with the step-of-5 rule). designs.understanding: models/founder.py forces name, email, phone, date_of_birth, gender, state, district and city to be NOT NULL, with unique email and phone, while the browser profile has every field optional. A partial profile cannot be saved, and the schema demands more personal data than the product needs. Founder.email duplicates users.email. Founder and Startup use SoftDeleteMixin with unique personal columns, so erasure keeps the data and blocks signing up again. completeness.py marks every present basic field as 'verified', and tier 100 'investment_ready' follows a client 'Documents verified (demo)' checkbox. The planned 'transparent' AES wrap of phone and email would break their unique indexes, and there is no key separate from the JWT secret_key. The root cause: the schema was written as a full profile form, with no notion of provenance (self-reported versus verified), minimisation, hard erasure or searchable encryption.

approaches.name: Minimal nullable schema, per-field provenance, hard delete, and an AES-GCM TypeDecorator with keyring and HMAC blind-index columns

HMAC-SHA256 blind indexes (separate BLIND_INDEX_KEY) serve phone and any lookup field, with uniqueness on the blind index. Completeness reports present fields and a separate verified list that only server checks may fill; tiers are renamed basic, standard and complete.
approaches.basis: cryptography (already installed through python-jose) AESGCM; the blind-index pattern (CipherSweet, Paragon IE) is a standard answer to searchable encryption.
approaches.advantages: Fixes sync, minimisation, erasure, honest verification and encryption together, offline, with keys separate from JWT signing and support for rotation.
approaches.drawbacks: One extra column per lookup field; key management is the operator's job (documented).

designs.understanding: Claim (seats.py) has no criterion, so synthesis.py picks the best or worst criterion and then speaks that seat's claims[0], whatever the claim was about; a neutral claim can be read out as 'the weakest point'. vote.weights_for adds technical +5 when no substring of a short TECH_SKILLS list appears in founder_skills, including when the skills are unknown (an enrichment slot the budget rarely reaches). So 'python developer' and 'never asked' both become 'no technical skill recorded'. council.convene makes one judge call per seat (seven, in parallel), each with the same full pack in the system prompt (model.py _system calls pack.lines() with no kinds), so the 'own slice' docstring is false. Failures are not recorded on the provider breaker, so a quota-exhausted Gemini costs the full 8 s on every run. The root cause: panel output is untyped where it matters (claim to criterion, skill to known or unknown), and the panel is shaped as seven independent model calls instead of one structured judgement that code then splits.

Rules seats give each claim a criterion, and synthesis picks the claim whose criterion matches. The call goes through the egress gate with priority 'panel' and records failures on the provider breaker. weights_for uses a three-state skill check: known technical, known non-technical, or unknown (no bump).

approaches.advantages: One request instead of seven per run; an explicit, testable claim-criterion pairing; an honest weights_why; and the tagged question feeds T05.
approaches.drawbacks: One failure loses every seat's opinion (rules stand in, as today); a longer output per call.

design.components: council/seats.py: Claim gains criterion (a Literal of CRITERIA); Opinion.ask_founder becomes Question{criterion, text, duplicates_slot}; validate() drops claims whose criterion is unknown or absent from the opinion's scores. council/model.py: ask_panel(client, pack, idea, slots, provider) -> (list[raw], usage), one call with per-seat briefs and a JSON schema (responseSchema for Gemini, the schema in the prompt for other providers). council/__init__.py: one gate.call(priority='panel') with an 8-10 s cap; on failure, breaker.fail() and rules for every seat; missing seats in a partial result are filled by rules. council/rules.py: every claim and question carries a criterion, and the customer question carries duplicates_slot='beneficiary'. council/synthesis.py: picks the first claim of the best or worst seat whose criterion matches, else states the score with no reason. council/vote.py: the question comes from the most-disputed criterion, else the weakest one, and is skipped if its duplicates_slot is filled; weights_for uses technical_skill(slots) -> True|False|None.
design.data_model: Claim{criterion: Literal['need','feasibility','compliance','economics','differentiation'], text, evidence}. Question{criterion, text, duplicates_slot: str|None}. The vote's 'question' becomes {criterion, text, from_seat, duplicates_slot}. Stored council results stay readable (an upgrader maps a string ask_founder to a Question with criterion None). The technical-skill vocabulary (software, developer, programmer, python, java, electronics, embedded, CAD, machinist, engineer, ...) lives in T01's vocabulary module, together with negative entries (non-technical roles) for the 'known non-technical' state.
design.algorithm: technical_skill: skills unknown (slot empty) -> None, no bump, and weights_why says 'founder's technical skills not known yet'; a Lexicon match of the technical vocabulary on word boundaries -> True, no bump; skills given and none matching -> False, +5 with the reason 'no technical skill among the skills you named'. Panel call: the prompt lists each seat's id, brief and focus kinds; the output is validated per seat, duplicate or unknown seat ids are ignored, and must_oppose is still enforced. Synthesis for criterion c: take the claim with claim.criterion == c from the high or low seat; else from any seat scoring c in the same direction; else give no reason clause.
design.interfaces: T05: the tagged Question enters add_dynamic with binds={'criterion': c} and duplicates_slot. T15: the call goes through gate.call(priority='panel') and is the panel's only request. T25: the policy is passed in, and private means rules. T10/T01: the Lexicon and the skill vocabulary. T13: evidence-pack relevance is unchanged. T34: upgrader for the council result shape.
design.rollout: 1) Criteria on claims and questions (rules first, then the model prompt), and synthesis matching. 2) Three-state skills. 3) The single call, behind a setting PANEL_MODE=single|per_seat for one release to compare outputs on the eval set; then per_seat is removed.
design.offline: Rules seats with criteria give a full panel offline; the single call is optional.

designs.tests: Unit: a claim with criterion 'economics' is never quoted for 'need'; rules seats always tag a criterion; a claim with no criterion is dropped. weights_for: skills None -> no bump; ['python developer'] -> no bump; ['tailoring'] -> +5 with the honest reason. Panel: a mocked provider returning a 7-opinion array gives seven opinions; a 5-opinion array gives two rules seats; a 429 calls breaker.fail and gives all rules; exactly one request is made (MockTransport counter). Eval set: the band and the question per idea stay stable between modes, within tolerance.
designs.risks: Less seat diversity from one call (mitigated by explicit per-seat briefs and the devil's advocate must_oppose rule). Small models may truncate the longer JSON (cap claims at 3 per seat, max_tokens about 1800). Gemini responseSchema field names vary by API version (keep a prompt-only fallback).
